title: setWindowDuration does not call _syncBudget, so in-flight dispatcher mintDebt is excluded from the rate recomputation and the new rate under-counts available budget
description: `setWindowDuration` calls `_updatePool()` (settles accrual) but does NOT call `_syncBudget()` (does not pull outstanding mint-debt from the dispatcher hook). It then recomputes `rewardRate = rewardBudget / newDuration`, using whatever `rewardBudget` is sitting on-contract. Any mint-debt that has accrued on the dispatcher side — which `totalBudget()` explicitly includes in the reported on-chain + pending sum — is excluded from the rate recomputation. The resulting per-second rate under-states the true available supply. When the dispatcher is eventually pulled later (via a user action), the window resets anyway and the 'new duration' the owner just set can be silently overridden depending on inflow magnitude.
economicImpact: The rate the owner sets does not reflect the full pot. If the dispatcher has accumulated X phUSD of mint-debt when the owner calls `setWindowDuration(newDuration)`, the rate is set to `rewardBudget / newDuration` instead of `(rewardBudget + X) / newDuration`. The difference either (a) under-emits until the next `_syncBudget` call, which then re-expands the window unexpectedly, or (b) results in the rate jumping upward right after the duration change — making the duration change opaque to off-chain monitoring. `runwaySeconds()` computes against `rewardBudget + mintDebt`, so any UI promising a runway will immediately mis-match the on-chain schedule.
attackPath: N/A — owner operator footgun, not an adversarial exploit. The mismatch between `setWindowDuration`'s rate and `totalBudget() / runwaySeconds()` views makes owner operations less predictable and can be exploited by a JIT-staker who times entry to the next post-setWindowDuration sync call to capture the back-loaded rate jump.
quantifiedLoss: Bounded by `dispatcherHook.mintDebt() / newDuration * stake-weight`. Non-adversarial in typical operation; affects transparency and predictability more than direct loss.
recommendation: Have `setWindowDuration` call `_syncBudget()` (not just `_updatePool()`) before recomputing the rate, so the new rate is derived from the complete budget including pending mint-debt. Consider also snapshot-logging the effective `(rewardBudget, rewardRate, windowEnd)` in the emitted event so operators can reconcile intent against state.
affectedParties: Owner / operator (predictability); minor MEV surface for JIT-stakers timing the next sync.
